title: Samson Hits 100 T20I Sixes as West Indies Level Series in Hyderabad Thriller
excerpt: Sanju Samson's 56 off 23 balls brought up both his 100th T20I six and India's 2,000th, but Shai Hope's unbeaten century and Keemo Paul's five wickets gave West Indies a 24-run win.
body:
• West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad, posting 247/3 and restricting India to 223/9 to level the five-match series 2-2.
  • Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls and became the sixth Indian to reach 100 sixes in T20 internationals, finishing the match on 102.
  • One of Samson's sixes was also India's 2,000th in T20Is, making India only the second team, after West Indies, to reach that mark.
  • Shai Hope made an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls and Keemo Paul took five wickets; the series decider is in Bengaluru on October 17.

Sanju Samson reached 100 sixes in Twenty20 internationals on Wednesday, but the milestone came in defeat as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth T20I at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad to level the five-match series at 2-2.

Hope sets an imposing target

Put in to bat after India won the toss, West Indies raced through the powerplay and never slowed. Captain Shai Hope finished unbeaten on 102 off 50 balls, with four fours and nine sixes, completing his century off the final delivery of the innings, according to Cricbuzz. It was his second century of the series.

Sherfane Rutherford supported him with an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls in an unbroken stand of 91, while Shimron Hetmyer struck 33 off just 12 balls. West Indies closed on 247/3, their second-highest T20I total against India. Prince Yadav and Axar Patel took a wicket each for India, but no bowler was able to contain the scoring for long.

Samson's double milestone

Samson gave the chase a fierce start, reaching his half-century off 20 balls and making 56 off 23, with six fours and four sixes. During that innings he passed 100 sixes in T20 internationals, becoming the sixth Indian to do so, behind Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav, Abhishek Sharma, Hardik Pandya and Virat Kohli, and ending the match with 102.

His six over long-off against Roston Chase in the third over carried a second record: it was India's 2,000th six in T20 internationals. India reached the mark in 297 matches, becoming the second team to do so after West Indies.

Paul breaks the chase

The turning point came when Keemo Paul struck with his first ball, removing Samson, and dismissed Ishan Kishan three balls later. Gudakesh Motie then removed Abhishek Sharma, who made 29 off 24, and Naman Dhir in successive deliveries, leaving India 130/5.

Tilak Varma, with 43 off 25, and Nitish Reddy, with 41 off 20, added 70 and briefly revived the chase, as reported by RevSportz. Paul returned in the 19th over to take three more wickets and finish with five, and India closed on 223/9 in 19.3 overs, with Arshdeep Singh retiring hurt. Cricbuzz noted it was the first time West Indies had beaten India in India while defending a total in T20Is, after six previous failed attempts.

Decider in Bengaluru

The series now moves to the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru on Saturday, October 17, with the trophy level at 2-2. India will need to solve the short-ball plan that stalled their middle order, while West Indies head into the finale with Hope in prolific form and Paul as the form bowler of the series.
